sources.notes: MIT OCW course identity for computability and computational complexity theory, including regular and context-free languages, decidable and undecidable problems, reducibility, recursive functions, time and space measures, completeness, hierarchy theorems, oracles, probabilistic computation, and interactive proof systems.

Lecture-note index for finite automata, regular expressions, CFGs, PDAs, Turing machines, Church-Turing thesis, decidability, undecidability, reducibility, recursion theorem, time complexity, P, NP, SAT, and polynomial-time reducibility; PDFs and PPTs remain child-resource boundaries.

MIT OCW course identity for theoretical CS spanning finite automata, circuits, decision trees, Turing machines, computability, efficient algorithms, reducibility, P versus NP, NP-completeness, randomness, cryptography, computational learning theory, and quantum computing.

Lecture-note index for DFAs, NFAs, regular expressions, pumping lemma, Turing machines, decidability, PCP, mapping reducibility, Rice's theorem, complexity theory, NP-completeness, probabilistic Turing machines, and complexity classes; PDFs remain child-resource boundaries.
